These are complete fixed-checker source captures, generated by unmodified
`rust/tools/check_selfdrive_state.py` on CPython 3.12.15. Before any replacement
candidate existed, the capture intercepted the subprocess boundary after the
original checker evaluated all 51,023 rows. The capture peer forwards those
independent original responses only to let the original checker finish its
artifact/report path. It contributes no policy or expected results.

`corpus.json.gz` contains exact `input.jsonl` and `source.json` bytes plus the
same independent responses serialized as JSON lines. `manifest.json` records
interpreter, source pins, compressed/uncompressed hashes and size. Repeating
the capture reproduced all five fixture files byte for byte.

`failures.json` records 17 child/candidate cases. `io-failures.json` records
six original artifact/print failure boundaries. The Rust integration tests
exercise the four boundaries available after the Runner seam; the two
pre-child input/source write failures remain independently recorded.
`cli.json` records help/argument exit statuses, not argparse diagnostic text.

Only the fixed checker is retired. The generic runtime `state.py`, `events.py`
and `realtime.py` remain live and mandatory drift pins. A missing or changed
runtime source fails before candidate execution; only the retired checker may
be absent. The Rust executable does not execute Python.

Parent verification passes four checker tests (30 seconds), 25 affected CI
policy/routing tests, scoped strict Clippy and the actual selfdrive_state example
build. The real original/native commands produce identical five artifact files,
stdout and stderr for all 51,023 cases. After source deletion, the native command
repeats every byte with PATH=/nonexistent; all four checker tests pass again.
Evidence is retained in `.analysis/scratch/2026-10-18-selfdrive-state/`.
